notes: Nine home flatbed scans of one woman, 1912-1974, to be brought to one quiet archival look. Four were scanned inside album mounts or a deckled border, so the picture sits a degree or two off level INSIDE a mount that is square to the glass and an auto-level locks to the mount and reports success while nothing moved. Two colour prints have lost most of one dye layer and their residual casts run in OPPOSITE directions, only legible once the fade is lifted. One print shows Ada's stove scar on her left hand, which must not be removed. Plus the retired framer's fixed-measure A6 caption card (longer captions clip at trim with no warning), a 10-row catalogue for 9 photographs (a duplicate, a contradicted date, a renamed file) and the family notes.

assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the retired Brattleboro framer's flat press PDF (caption card) to be authored/rendered downstream. Six of these are already hanging, so the new cards must match this layout exactly.

Document: single page, A6 LANDSCAPE (148 x 105 mm), 4 mm safety, fonts embedded. Shows a 2019 caption (short, two or three words) so the new, longer captions must be re-mapped and their fit re-checked.

GEOMETRY:
- GRAPHIC FRAME (small placed reference thumbnail): left, ~34 x 45 mm, one linked image with an integer page-item id.
- TEXT FRAME (right column) - a SINGLE continuous story, one FIXED-MEASURE frame roughly 95 x 62 mm that does NOT auto-grow and does NOT show overset warnings. Runs in this order:
    Run 1 (TITLE): quiet text serif, ~15 pt. 2019 value: "Ada, 1912"
    Run 2 (DATE AND PLACE): serif, ~10 pt, one line. 2019 value: "Brattleboro"
    Run 3 (NAMES): serif, ~10 pt, one line. 2019 value: "Ada Hollis"
    Run 4 (PROVENANCE): serif ITALIC, ~9 pt, one line, its own paragraph run inside the same story. 2019 value: "Studio card."

Field labels the downstream mapping must resolve (as content, not visible tokens): TITLE, DATE_PLACE, NAMES, PROVENANCE, THUMB.

Colours: Paper White #F5F1E9 ground, Archive Black #191613 title, Ink Charcoal #33302B body, Museum Grey #6F6B64 provenance italic.

Because the 2019 captions were two or three words, the framer sized the text frame tightly. A record whose NAMES run carries three names and whose DATE_PLACE run carries a town and a year will overflow the fixed measure: the overset text is simply absent from the render at trim while the page count stays correct and the screen proof looks like a finished card. The provenance is a run inside the single flow, not a separate frame, so field offsets must be computed against the reconstructed story.

assets.content:
WHAT WE KNOW, AND WHAT WE DO NOT WANT TOUCHED
Typed by Ruth (Ada's daughter). Two pages, kept since the nineties.

The photographs, oldest first:
- 1912, Brattleboro. Ada as a baby. The oldest one, a studio card, in the black album.
- 1931, Brattleboro. Ada as a young woman, in the album too.
- The wedding of Ada and Walter. The catalogue says 1938 but the back of the print is written in Ada's own hand "June 1936", and Mother was always sure of it. Use 1936.
- 1948, the porch, Ada with me as a baby.
- 1955, Putney, Ada with the three of us (me, Frank and Carol) in front of the old house. NOTE: cousin Dale sent this same photograph round again a few years ago under his own name for it and with the year as 1956. It is the SAME picture. We only need it once.
- 1967, the garden. Gone very orange.
- 1971, at the stove. This is the one with the SCAR on Nan's left hand, from the stove years before. A reprint somebody paid for in the eighties took the scar out and I have never forgiven it. The scar STAYS. Do not remove it, do not tidy it, do not smooth it.
- 1969, Nan with baby Tom.
- 1974, Nan in the garden chair, near the end.

Things that are the photograph, not damage, and must stay: the scar; the grain; the paper texture and deckled edges; the little pencil retouching the old studio did on Nan's cheek in the 1931 card; anything actually in the picture.

Quiet, please. Like a museum, not a memory book. Tell us what you corrected and what you left, and why.
